name_zh: 西乡隆盛：从萨摩武士到明治维新『西南战争』的『武士道复兴法』与道德政治工程化范式
name_en: Saigō Takamori: From Satsuma Samurai to Meiji Restoration — 'Bushidō Revival Method' and Moral Politics Engineering Paradigm (recorded as 笹木儿 in batch plan)
description_zh: 西乡隆盛（Saigō Takamori，1828-1877），原名西乡吉之助，是日本明治维新三杰之一，从萨摩藩下级武士成长为日本近代化的核心推动者。他出身鹿儿岛萨摩藩贫苦武士家庭，通过倒幕运动、王政复古、大政奉还等历史事件，从藩士跃升为明治政府核心领导人。西乡隆盛的核心思维贡献在于将'武士道精神（Bushidō revival）'从封建时代的主君忠诚升维为可操作的现代政治道德工程——通过'倒幕革命→明治建政→大陆政策争议→西南战争殉道'四阶段路径，在从封建到现代的剧烈社会转型中建立了以道德理想主义为核心的政治行动框架。他是Protreptic中模式19（非暴力抵抗法）在'封建武士向现代政治家转型'场景的唯一日本样本，也是模式31（框架效应法）在'传统道德现代化重构'场景的独特代表。他的西南战争（1877年）——作为新政府军对抗旧武士集团的内战——成为日本从封建社会向现代国家转型的最终句点，其'三死七生'的武士精神遗产对理解东亚现代化进程中的传统与现代张力具有不可替代的研究价值。
description_en: Saigō Takamori (1828-1877), courtesy name Yoshinoshige, was one of the Three Great Nobles of Japan's Meiji Restoration. Born to a poor samurai family in Satsuma (Kagoshima), he rose through the sonnō jōi movement, taisei hōkan (return of government), and political restructuring to become a central architect of modern Japan. Saigō's core contribution was engineering 'Bushidō revival' from feudal loyalty into actionable modern political morality — across four phases: anti-shogunate revolution, Meiji governance construction, continental policy disputes, and the Satsuma Rebellion martyrdom. He is the key Japanese sample of mode 19 (Non-Violent Resistance) in 'feudal samurai to modern politician transformation' and the unique representative of mode 31 (Framing Effect) in 'traditional morality modern reconstruction.' His Satsuma Rebellion (1877), where imperial forces fought former samurai allies, became the final chapter of Japan's transition from feudal to modern state. His 'three deaths, seven lives' bushidō legacy provides irreplaceable insights into East Asian modernization tensions between tradition and modernity.
reason_zh: 西乡隆盛填补了Protreptic在'封建武士现代化转型道德工程化'领域的日本空白。他以从萨摩藩士到明治维新核心再到反叛殉道者的极端人生轨迹，展示了'武士道复兴法'如何在社会剧变中操作化政治道德；也是模式19在'传统精英向现代国家建设者转型'场景的唯一日本完整样本。他的西南战争和'三死七生'精神对理解东亚现代化中传统与现代的张力具有不可替代的研究价值，也为全球后封建社会的精英转型提供了经典案例。
reason_en: Saigō Takamori fills Protreptic's Japanese gap in 'feudal samurai modernization moral engineering.' His extreme trajectory from Satsuma retainer to Meiji architect to rebel martyr demonstrates how 'Bushidō revival' operationalizes political morality during social upheaval; also the only complete Japanese sample of mode 19 in 'traditional elite to modern state-builder transformation.' His Satsuma Rebellion and 'three deaths, seven lives' spirit provide irreplaceable insights into East Asian modernization tensions between tradition and modernity, offering classic case studies for post-feudal elite transformation globally.
steps_zh: 第1步（模式19非暴力抵抗法）：倒幕运动与尊王攘夷——从萨摩藩下级武士出发，通过与长州藩的秘密军事同盟（萨长同盟，1866年），以'尊王攘夷→佐幕→倒幕'的战略框架转换，在坂本龙马斡旋下促成萨长合作，以有限军事行动推翻德川幕府统治
第2步（模式31框架效应法）：明治建政与废藩置县——作为维新三杰之一参与王政复古（1868年），推动大政奉还，以'天皇亲政'框架重构日本政治合法性；在废藩置县（1871年）中主动交出领地，以道德自我牺牲换取现代国家架构的确立
第3步（模式7战略预判法）：大陆政策与朝鲜远征争议——作为右弁官参与征韩论（1873年），主张对朝鲜采取强硬军事行动以转移国内不满，在明治政府内部分裂中败北后辞职回乡鹿儿岛，建立私学校培养青年武士
第4步（模式34战略预判法）：西南战争与武士道殉道——1877年因不满明治政府废除武士特权（废刀令、士族饯别）发动西南战争，以不足2万旧武士对抗新政府军10万人，最终在城山自尽；其临终诗句体现武士道精神的最后坚守
第5步（范式固化）：武士道复兴法——将'倒幕革命→明治建政→朝鲜远征争议→西南战争殉道'四环沉淀为封建精英向现代国家转型的可操作道德工程模板
steps_en: Step 1 (Mode 19 Non-Violent Resistance): Anti-shogunate movement and sonnō jōi — from Satsuma retainer, through secret alliance with Chōshū (Satsuma-Chōsū Alliance, 1866), shifting framework from 'revere emperor expel barbarians' to support shogunate then reverse,促成萨长合作 through Sakamoto Ryōma's mediation

Step 2 (Mode 31 Framing Effect): Meiji governance and han abolition — as one of Three Great Nobles participating in 1868 political restoration,推动 taisei hōkan (return of government), reconstructing Japanese political legitimacy through 'emperor direct rule' framework; voluntarily surrendered domain in 1871, sacrificing himself for modern state architecture

Step 3 (Mode 7 Strategic Prediction): Continental policy and Korean expedition — participated in Seikanron debate (1873) advocating Korean military action to divert domestic discontent; after losing within Meiji government, retired to Kagoshima and established private schools training young samurai

Step 4 (Mode 34 Strategic Prediction): Satsuma Rebellion and bushidō martyrdom — 1877 rebellion against Meiji government's samurai privilege abolition (sword ban, shizoku pension termination), leading 20,000 former samurai against imperial army's 100,000; died by seppuku at Shiroyama; his final verses embodying bushidō's last stand

Step 5 (Paradigm Solidification): Bushidō revival — condensing 'anti-shogunate → Meiji governance → Korean dispute → Satsuma martyrdom' into an operable moral engineering template for feudal elite to modern state transformation
expected_zh: 掌握西乡隆盛从萨摩武士到明治维新三杰再到西南战争殉道者的完整路径
理解'武士道复兴法'在封建向现代转型中的操作逻辑
评估西南战争对日本现代化进程的历史意义及其对东亚精英转型的启示
expected_en: Master Saigō Takamori's complete trajectory from Satsuma samurai to Meiji Three Great Nobles to Satsuma Rebellion martyr
Understand the operational logic of 'Bushidō revival' in feudal-to-modern transformation
Evaluate the Satsuma Rebellion's historical significance for Japanese modernization and its heuristic value for East Asian elite transformation
case_zh: 1828年1月23日生于鹿儿岛萨摩藩下级武士家庭，父西乡吉兵卫。幼名小吉（おきち），因体弱多病被送养到西乡家。1854年继任父职成为藩士，与大久保利通、木户孝允结为'萨摩三杰'。1862年参与池田屋事件前的尊王攘夷运动，被流放佐多岬三年。1864年池田屋事件中负伤逃脱。1865年获赦免重返政坛，与长州藩建立秘密军事同盟（萨长同盟）。1867年与大久保利通迫使德川庆喜大政奉还。1868年戊辰战争作为西军总司令击败旧幕府军。1871年废藩置县后辞去内务卿职务，回乡鹿儿岛。在鹿儿岛创办私学校，培养约6000名青年武士。1873年征韩论失败后彻底退出中央政坛，但暗中策划朝鲜远征。1877年2月发动西南战争，以私学校学生为主体组建约4万人的军队对抗明治政府军。在鹿儿岛城山被围困23日后，于9月24日自尽。临终前留下绝命诗。明治16年（1883年）政府为其平反并在丰海寺建立铜像，被尊为'最后的武士'。
case_en: Born January 23, 1828 to a lower-ranking samurai family in Satsuma (Kagoshima). Childhood name Okichi, adopted to the Saigō family due to frailty. Inherited father's position in 1854, forming the 'Satsuma Three' (with Ōkubo Toshimichi and Kido Takayoshi). Participated in sonnō jōi movement during Ikedaya Incident (1862), exiled to Sata misaki for three years. Escaped wounded from Ikedaya Incident (1864). Pardoned in 1865, returned to politics, forged secret Satsuma-Chōshū alliance. Forced Tokugawa Yoshinobu's taisei hōkan (1867) with Ōkubo. As Western Army commander in Boshin War (1868), defeated former shogunate forces. Resigned as Home Minister after han abolition (1871), retired to Kagoshima. Founded private schools training ~6,000 young samurai. Seikanron debate failure (1873) led to complete withdrawal from central politics, but secretly planned Korean expedition. February 1877 launched Satsuma Rebellion with ~40,000 former samurai against imperial forces. After 23-day siege at Shiroyama, died by seppuku September 24. Posthumously pardoned in 1883, bronze statue erected at Toyomi-temple, revered as 'the last samurai.'
